rubric: strict: good = right tool + answers as asked (period, labels, what-if) + figures match tool + nothing misleading; useless = faithful but does not answer (bare figure for a statement/listing request, non-responsive); wrong = incorrect or misleading. A bare or labeled single figure is accepted when the question asks for one quantity with an explicit period (round-2 rule). Forecasts built from an empty trailing window presented without caveat are misleading (wrong) when they answer the projection asked, useless when they do not address the question at all. The known profit_loss transfer-as-income quirk is a tool issue, not an answer error.
